question: A 12-month-old boy who presents a right testicle in the inguinal canal during health examinations performed since birth, and it is not possible to descend to the scrotum. Point out the CORRECT answer:

options.opa: The most probable diagnosis is the retractable testicle.
options.opb: It is necessary to wait until two years of age to occur spontaneous descent of it.
options.opc: Human chorionic gonadotropin is the treatment of first choice.
options.opd: The indication of orchidopexy should not be deferred.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "12-month-old boy with right testicle in inguinal canal" -> "testicle not descended to scrotum" -> "likely diagnosis of undescended testicle" -> "orchidopexy is indicated" -> "deferring treatment can lead to complications" -> 85%

CHAIN: "12-month-old boy with right testicle in inguinal canal" -> "testicle not descended to scrotum" -> "retractable testicle is unlikely" -> "orchidopexy is the recommended treatment" -> "waiting until two years is not necessary" -> 90%

CHAIN: "12-month-old boy with right testicle in inguinal canal" -> "testicle not descended to scrotum" -> "human chorionic gonadotropin is not first-line treatment" -> "orchidopexy is the standard approach" -> "indication for surgery should not be deferred" -> 80%

CHAIN: "12-month-old boy with right testicle in inguinal canal" -> "testicle not descended to scrotum" -> "spontaneous descent is unlikely after 6 months" -> "orchidopexy is the appropriate intervention" -> "deferring treatment can lead to infertility" -> 90%
analysis: The clinical presentation suggests that the boy has an undescended testicle (cryptorchidism), which is not retractable since it cannot be manually descended into the scrotum. Waiting until two years of age is not advisable as the risk of complications increases. Human chorionic gonadotropin can be used in some cases, but it is not the first-line treatment. Orchidopexy is the recommended treatment for undescended testicles and should not be delayed.
